fullPassage:
[P01] A familiar song can remain interesting even when listeners know most of its melody. Their knowledge of familiar patterns gives them expectations that a performer can either satisfy or gently disturb. Suppose a singer repeats a short phrase several times and then holds its final note longer than before. The change feels meaningful partly because the earlier repetitions taught listeners when the note should end. Without that pattern, the extra length might not stand out at all. This helps explain why musical surprise is different from a collection of unrelated sounds. A surprise needs an expectation to depart from, while a completely unpredictable sequence offers little basis for anticipation. On the other hand, a performance that follows every expectation exactly may soon feel mechanical. An effective balance between these extremes creates emotional interest. The performer establishes enough order for the audience to follow, then introduces unexpected changes that make them listen more closely. The emotional value of music therefore depends not simply on the presence of something new, but on the relationship between what happens and what they were prepared to hear.

[P02] A business does not always reduce costs by using less of every resource. An effective business often makes changes to the balance of resources it uses. Imagine two small furniture companies that make similar tables. One operates in a town where workshop space is inexpensive, while the other works in a city where rent is high. The first company can afford to keep large supplies of wood and finished tables on site. The second may order materials more frequently and produce tables only after customers request them. This approach could increase delivery costs and require more careful planning. Nevertheless, it may be cheaper overall because it reduces the amount of costly space the company needs. What looks inefficient when one expense is considered alone can be efficient when all expenses are compared. There is therefore no single arrangement that is best for every business in every place. The value of an arrangement depends on the relationship between local prices and total costs. When one resource becomes expensive, a successful business may use more of another to achieve the same result at a lower total cost.

[P03] Free time may seem like something people obtain only after they become wealthy. However, it can also emerge when they become more effective at meeting basic needs. Imagine an early human group whose members search for food separately. Each person must discover where food is available and face the risks of collecting it. If they begin sharing information, watching seasonal changes, and dividing tasks, the same amount of food may require fewer hours of effort. Their advantage comes from organizing knowledge rather than simply increasing physical strength. Under favorable conditions, the time saved can be spent making tools, telling stories, or playing with children. Such activities are possible because survival no longer demands every available moment. This freedom is not guaranteed: a shortage of food can quickly consume it again. Still, the example shows why material abundance alone does not fully explain leisure. A group can gain time by changing how it works, even without greatly increasing what it owns. Greater intelligence and cooperation can therefore create opportunities that constant individual effort cannot.

[P04] During a frightening event, silence may occur before a person has consciously decided to remain quiet. A sudden unfamiliar noise can cause someone to stop moving, listen closely, and find speaking unexpectedly difficult. These reactions can be understood as parts of a protective response. Movement and sound might reveal a person's location, while stillness allows attention to be directed toward possible danger. From this perspective, the temporary loss of words is not necessarily a failure of language ability. A system concerned with immediate safety is interrupting an activity that might make the person easier to notice. Once the surroundings seem safe, movement and conversation can return. The difficulty arises when the sense of danger continues after the immediate threat has passed. A response that helps someone through a brief emergency may interfere with ordinary life if it remains active. Understanding this difference matters when we judge another person's silence. The question is not only whether that person knows what to say, but also whether their body currently allows them to say it.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 주변이 '안전해(safe)' 보일 때 움직임과 대화가 돌아오므로 ③ dangerous는 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ dangerous 가 부적절 — 뒤에 '움직임과 대화가 돌아온다'고 했으므로 주변이 '안전해(safe)' 보이는 상황이어야 한다.
❌ ① difficult : 말하기가 갑자기 '어려워진다'는 맥락에 맞다.
❌ ② protective : 멈춤·침묵이 '보호' 반응이라는 맥락에 맞다.
❌ ④ interfere : 위험 감각이 지속되면 일상을 '방해'한다는 맥락에 맞다.
det.tip: safe ↔ dangerous. 돌아오는 상황은 안전할 때이다.

det.korean: 반복이 끝 음의 길이에 '의미(meaningful)'를 부여하는 맥락이므로 ② meaningless는 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② meaningless 가 부적절 — 바로 뒤에서 '앞선 반복이 언제 음이 끝날지 알려 주기 때문에' 변화가 느껴진다고 했으므로 변화는 '의미 있게(meaningful)' 느껴져야 한다.
❌ ① interesting : 익숙한 노래도 흥미로울 수 있다는 맥락에 맞다.
❌ ③ mechanical : 기대를 그대로 따르는 연주가 '기계적'이라는 맥락에 맞다.
❌ ④ new : 가치가 '새로움'의 존재에만 달린 것은 아니라는 맥락에 맞다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 한 자원이 비싸지면 다른 자원을 더 써서 더 낮은 비용으로 '같은 결과(the same result)'를 얻는다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ the same result(같은 결과) : 핵심은 '더 낮은 총비용으로 동일한 결과'를 얻는 자원 대체이므로 the same result가 맞다.
❌ ① a bigger profit(더 큰 이익) : 본문은 이익 증대가 아니라 비용 절감을 말한다.
❌ ② more free space(더 많은 여유 공간) : 공간은 수단일 뿐 목표가 아니다.
❌ ③ faster delivery(더 빠른 배송) : 오히려 배송비가 늘 수 있다고 했다.
det.tip: use more of another → 같은 결과를 더 싸게.

det.korean: 정보 공유·분업을 하면 같은 양의 식량에 '더 적은 시간(fewer hours)'이 든다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① fewer hours(더 적은 시간) : 정보를 공유하고 과업을 나누면 같은 식량을 얻는 데 '더 적은 시간'의 노력이 든다는 흐름이다.
❌ ② more workers(더 많은 노동자) : 인원 증가가 아니라 효율이 핵심이다.
❌ ③ greater strength(더 큰 힘) : 뒤에서 '체력 증가가 아니다'라고 한다.
❌ ④ higher risks(더 높은 위험) : 위험은 줄어드는 방향이다.
det.tip: 효율 향상 → fewer hours of effort.

가만히 있는 것은 주의를 가능한 위험으로 향하게 한다.
공포 상황의 침묵은 항상 언어 능력의 영구적 상실을 뜻한다.
위협이 지난 뒤에도 위험 느낌이 계속되면 문제가 생긴다.

❌ ② 일치 : stillness allows attention to be directed toward possible danger.
❌ ④ 일치 : difficulty arises when the sense of danger continues after the threat has passed.

ch: how leisure can arise from better organization and cooperation

questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: Why We Must Always Keep Speaking During Danger
Silence as the Body's Protective Response to Fear
A Complete History of Human Language Development
Simple Tips to Overcome the Fear of Public Speaking

det.korean: 공포 상황의 침묵이 언어 능력의 실패가 아니라 '몸의 보호 반응'이라는 것이 제목으로 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② Silence as the Body's Protective Response to Fear(공포에 대한 몸의 보호 반응으로서의 침묵) : 본문의 핵심 주장을 담은 제목이다.
❌ ① Why We Must Always Keep Speaking During Danger(위험 중 늘 말해야 하는 이유) : 본문과 반대이다.
❌ ③ A History of Human Language Development(언어 발달의 역사) : 다루지 않은 내용이다.
❌ ④ Tips to Overcome Fear of Public Speaking(발표 공포 극복 팁) : 주제가 아니다.
det.tip: silence = protective response, not language failure.

questions.passage: Free time may seem like something people obtain only after they become wealthy. However, it can also emerge when they become more effective at meeting basic needs. Imagine an early human group whose members search for food separately. Each person must discover where food is available and face the risks of collecting it. If they begin sharing information, watching seasonal changes, and dividing tasks, the same amount of food may require fewer hours of effort. Their advantage comes from organizing knowledge rather than simply increasing physical strength. Under favorable conditions, the time saved can be spent making tools, telling stories, or playing with children. Such activities are possible because survival no longer demands every available moment. This freedom is not guaranteed: a shortage of food can quickly <u>consume it again</u>. Still, the example shows why material abundance alone does not fully explain leisure. A group can gain time by changing how it works, even without greatly increasing what it owns. Greater intelligence and cooperation can therefore create opportunities that constant individual effort cannot.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>consume it again</u>이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: literally eat the gathered food once more
greatly increase the group's physical strength
permanently end all human cooperation and sharing
quickly use up the free time the group had gained

det.korean: 여기서 it은 '자유 시간'을 가리키고 consume은 '써 버리다/앗아가다'를 뜻한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ quickly use up the free time the group had gained(얻었던 자유 시간을 빠르게 써 버린다) : 앞 문장의 '자유는 보장되지 않는다'와 연결되어, 식량 부족이 어렵게 얻은 '여가 시간'을 다시 앗아간다는 뜻이다.
❌ ① literally eat the food(문자 그대로 음식을 먹는다) : consume을 글자 그대로 해석한 오답이다.
❌ ② increase physical strength(체력을 키운다) : 무관하다.
❌ ③ end all cooperation(모든 협력을 끝낸다) : 과장·무관이다.
det.tip: it = free time, consume = 써 버리다/앗아가다.

questions.passage: A business does not always reduce costs by using less of every resource. An effective business often makes changes to the balance of resources it uses. Imagine two small furniture companies that make similar tables. One operates in a town where workshop space is inexpensive, while the other works in a city where rent is high. The first company can afford to keep large supplies of wood and finished tables on site. The second may order materials more frequently and produce tables only after customers request them. This approach could increase delivery costs and require more careful planning. Nevertheless, <u>it</u> may be cheaper overall because it reduces the amount of costly space the company needs. What looks inefficient when one expense is considered alone can be efficient when all expenses are compared. There is therefore no single arrangement that is best for every business in every place. The value of an arrangement depends on the relationship between local prices and total costs. When one resource becomes expensive, a successful business may use more of another to achieve the same result at a lower total cost.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>it</u>이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 첫 번째 회사가 큰 재고를 두는 방식
두 번째 회사가 자재를 자주 주문하고 주문받은 뒤 생산하는 방식

det.korean: 밑줄 친 it은 앞서 설명한 '두 번째 회사의 주문형(on-demand) 운영 방식'을 가리킨다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 두 번째 회사의 방식 — 앞에서 '두 번째 회사는 자재를 더 자주 주문하고 주문 후에 생산한다'고 했고, 이것이 공간을 줄여 '전체적으로 더 저렴할 수 있다'고 이어지므로 it은 그 방식을 가리킨다.
❌ ① 첫 번째 회사의 방식은 큰 재고를 '두는' 방식으로, 저렴함의 근거가 아니다.
❌ ③ 높은 임대료는 오히려 비용 증가 요인이다.
❌ ④ 배송은 비용을 늘리는 요소로 언급된다.
det.tip: it = the second company's on-demand approach.

Imagine an early human group whose members search for food separately. Each person must discover where food is available and face the risks of collecting it. If they begin sharing information, watching seasonal changes, and dividing tasks, the same amount of food may require fewer hours of effort. Their advantage comes from organizing knowledge rather than simply increasing physical strength. Under favorable conditions, the time saved can be spent __________, telling stories, or playing with children. Such activities are possible because survival no longer demands every available moment. This freedom is not guaranteed: a shortage of food can quickly consume it again. Still, the example shows why material abundance alone does not fully explain leisure. A group can gain time by changing how it works, even without greatly increasing what it owns. Greater intelligence and cooperation can therefore create opportunities that constant individual effort cannot.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 절약된 시간은 '도구 만들기(making tools)', 이야기하기, 아이와 놀기 같은 활동에 쓰인다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ making tools(도구 만들기) : 뒤의 'telling stories, or playing with children'과 병렬되는, 생존을 넘어선 여가·창조 활동이어야 하므로 making tools가 맞다.
❌ ① hunting alone for more food(혼자 더 사냥하기) : 생존 활동으로 여가의 예와 어긋난다.
❌ ② gathering water(물 긷기) : 역시 생존 과업이다.
❌ ④ fighting against enemies(적과 싸우기) : 문맥과 무관하다.

questions.passage: __________ even when listeners know most of its melody. Their knowledge of familiar patterns gives them expectations that a performer can either satisfy or gently disturb.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]의 단어를 활용하여 빈칸에 알맞은 영어를 쓰시오. (영어로)
익숙한 노래는 흥미로운 상태를 유지할 수 있다.
[조건] (1) a, can, familiar, interesting, remain, song 중 필요한 단어를 골라 모두 사용할 것 (2) 정확히 6단어로 쓸 것
questions.wa: A familiar song can remain interesting
accept: A familiar song can remain interesting

det.korean: 주어 'A familiar song' + 조동사 can + 동사 remain + 보어 interesting으로 쓴다.
det.analysis: 'remain + 형용사(interesting)'는 '~한 상태를 유지하다'라는 2형식 구문이며, 조동사 can 뒤에 동사원형 remain을 쓴다.

questions.passage: A business does not always reduce costs by using less of every resource. An effective business often makes changes to the balance of resources it __________ (use).
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 관계절 'resources (that) it uses'에서 주어 it(단수)에 맞춰 현재시제 uses로 쓴다.
det.analysis: 목적격 관계절 'the resources it uses'로, 주어 it이 3인칭 단수 현재이므로 use → uses가 된다.

questions.passage: Still, the example shows why material abundance alone does not fully explain leisure. __________, even without greatly increasing what it owns.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]의 단어를 활용하여 빈칸에 알맞은 영어를 쓰시오. (영어로)
집단은 일하는 방식을 바꿈으로써 시간을 벌 수 있다.
[조건] (1) a, by, can, changing, gain, group, how, it, time, works 중 필요한 단어를 골라 모두 사용할 것 (2) 정확히 10단어로 쓸 것, 'by + 동명사' 구문을 사용할 것
questions.wa: A group can gain time by changing how it works
accept: A group can gain time by changing how it works

det.korean: 'by + 동명사(changing)'로 수단을 나타내고, 'how it works'를 목적어로 쓴다.
det.analysis: 주어 A group + can gain time 뒤에 수단의 'by changing how it works(일하는 방식을 바꿈으로써)'를 붙여 9단어로 완성한다. by 다음은 동명사 changing이다.

questions.passage: __________ One operates in a town where workshop space is inexpensive, while the other works in a city where rent is high. The first company can afford to keep large supplies of wood and finished tables on site.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 빈칸을 완성하시오. (영어로, 9단어)
비슷한 테이블을 만드는 두 개의 작은 가구 회사를 상상해 보라.
[단어] companies / furniture / Imagine / make / similar / small / tables / that / two
questions.wa: Imagine two small furniture companies that make similar tables
accept: Imagine two small furniture companies that make similar tables

det.korean: 명령문 Imagine + 목적어(two small furniture companies) + 관계절(that make similar tables) 순서이다.
det.analysis: 동사원형으로 시작하는 명령문이며, 형용사 어순은 수량(two)-크기(small)-명사(furniture companies)이고 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 절이 뒤따른다.

questions.passage: Movement and sound might reveal a person's location, while __________.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]의 단어를 활용하여 빈칸에 알맞은 영어를 쓰시오. (영어로)
가만히 있는 것은 주의가 가능한 위험으로 향하도록 해 준다.
[조건] (1) allows, attention, be, danger, directed, possible, stillness, to, toward 중 필요한 단어를 골라 모두 사용할 것 (2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것
questions.wa: stillness allows attention to be directed toward possible danger
accept: stillness allows attention to be directed toward possible danger

det.korean: 'allow + 목적어(attention) + to부정사'이며, attention은 '향해지는' 대상이라 수동 부정사 to be directed를 쓴다.
det.analysis: 'stillness allows attention to be directed ~' 구조로, allow A to-v의 to부정사가 수동(to be directed)이 되어 '주의가 향해지도록 허용한다'는 뜻이 된다.
det.tip: allow + 목적어 + to be p.p.(수동 부정사).
